article.title: Replay: Macron, Carney hail new chapter on France-Canada ties at St. Pierre and Miquelon meeting
article.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said France and Canada were "two great independent nations who want to stay that way" in a joint news conference with Canadian leader Mark Carney Sunday. Watch the press conference by the two leaders on the French overseas territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon just off Canada's Atlantic coast.

article.title: Macron heading to Saint Pierre and Miquelon to meet with Canadian PM Carney
article.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is travelling to Saint Pierre and Miquelon this weekend, an archipelago the Élysée describes as "central to today's France."

article.title: Macron reaffirms French sovereignty over Saint Pierre and Miquelon against Trump's ambitions
article.summary: Emmanuel Macron arrived in the French North Atlantic territory on Saturday, where he will receive Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. The visit signals Canada's intent to distance itself from the US under Donald Trump.

article.title: Macron, Carney hail new chapter in France-Canada ties at symbolic archipelago meeting
article.summary: French President ​Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on ​Sunday called for stronger bilateral ties in the face of new global threats at a meeting on Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a French territory off Canada's Newfoundland. The first-ever visit by a Canadian leader to the North Atlantic archipelago came as both countries have increasingly awkward relations with the US.

article.title: Macron touts relationship with Canada in visit to Saint Pierre and Miquelon
article.summary: Macron said he saw the planned meeting with Mark Carney as "a very strong gesture of friendship" and pointed to the Canadian leader's blossoming relationship with Brussels.

article.title: Macron, Carney to meet in French Atlantic archipelago in signal to Trump
article.summary: UNITED NATIONS, Sept 20 - President Emmanuel Macron visits the French territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon on Sunday, where he is due to meet Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, weeks after U.S. President Donald Trump posted an image on social media showing the archipelago covered by the American flag.
